```{r}
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(tigris)
library(units)
library(dplyr)


  
#1 - The file cb_2024_us_county_500k.shp is a shape file that includes shapes for all counties in the United States. Use it to draw a map of the counties of New York State (and only New York State - do not include counties from neighboring states).

#Read the Shapefile  
counties <- st_read("~/Desktop/cb_2024_us_county_500k.shp")

#Filter for New York State (FIPS 36).
ny_counties <- filter(counties, STATEFP == "36")

#Caculate the area of each county
ny_counties$area_m2 <- st_area(ny_counties)

#Convert the area of each county to square miles
ny_counties$area_sq_miles <- set_units(ny_counties$area_m2, "mi^2")

#Convert the area into plain numbers
ny_counties$area_sq_miles <- as.numeric(set_units(st_area(ny_counties), "mi^2"))

#Find the largest area for county
ny_counties$is_largest <- ny_counties$area_sq_miles == max(ny_counties$area_sq_miles)

# 2. Transform the shapefile to a geopackage
ny_gpkg <- st_read("~/Desktop/ny_counties.gpkg")

# 3. Create map for visualization using geom_sf()
ggplot(data = ny_gpkg) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = is_largest), color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "#FFFACD", "TRUE" = "#698B69"),
    labels = c("Other Counties", "Largest County (St. Lawrence)"),
    name = NULL) +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = NAME), size = 2) +
  ggtitle("Counties of New York State (2023)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}

#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)

Sys.setenv(CENSUS_API_KEY = "9c9c7d071c8c8424a701ad68cc0b7fc6aa835ce2")

# 1. Define the years to compare
years <- 2020:2023

# 2. Download NY county shapes once (so geometry downloads fast)
ny_shapes <- get_acs(
  geography = "county",
  variables = "B01003_001",
  state = "NY",
  year = 2023,
  geometry = TRUE
) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, geometry)

# 3. Loop get_acs() across 2020-2023 and attach the year to each row
ny_pop_time <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {
  get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    variables = "B01003_001",
    state = "NY",
    year = yr,
    geometry = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(year = yr)
})

# 4. Join the multi-year population data to the county shapes
ny_map_time <- ny_shapes %>%
  left_join(ny_pop_time, by = c("GEOID", "NAME"))

# 5. Plot all 4 years side-by-side with a shared color scale
ggplot(data = ny_map_time) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = estimate), color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#ffffcc",
    high = "#d94701",
    labels = comma,
    name = "Population"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 2) +
  ggtitle("County Population in New York State (2020–2023)") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5)
  )
```


```{r}
# 4. Table of county names, coordinates, and land area below the map
centers <- st_centroid(ny_gpkg)
coords <- st_coordinates(centers)

county_table <- st_drop_geometry(ny_gpkg) %>%
  mutate(
    latitude = round(coords[, "Y"], 4),
    longitude = round(coords[, "X"], 4),
    area_sq_miles = set_units(ALAND, "m^2") %>% 
    set_units("mi^2") %>% as.numeric() %>% round(1)) %>%
  select(County = NAME, Latitude = latitude, Longitude = longitude, `Area (sq mi)` = area_sq_miles) %>%
arrange(desc(`Area (sq mi)`))

knitr::kable(county_table)

# The largest county by area (square miles) in New York is St. Lawrence (2,680.3 sq mi)
```

```{r}

# 3 - Use nyshighpoints.csv to plot the location of high points of every county in New York over the base county map.

library(sf)
library(tidyverse)


#Read the CSV and convert to spatial sf object matching the base map CRS
highpoints_df <- read_csv("~/Desktop/nyshighpoints.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

highpoints_sf <- highpoints_df %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(ny_gpkg))

#Isolate the single highest high point in New York State
highest_point <- highpoints_sf %>%
  slice_max(Elevation_Meters, n = 1)

#Plot the base map, colored high points, and label the highest peak
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ny_gpkg, fill = "#CAE1FF", color = "gray55", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(
    data = highpoints_sf,
    aes(fill = Elevation_Meters),
    shape = 21,
    color = "black",
    size = 2.2,
    stroke = 0.4) +
  
  #Add a label above the highest point
  geom_sf_label(
    data = highest_point,
    aes(label = paste0("Highest Elevation - Mount Marcy (", Elevation_Meters, " m)")),
    nudge_y = 0.22,
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = "#FFFFE0",
    alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#54FF9F", "#f4d03f", "#FF6A6A", "#B22222", "#CD00CD"),
    name = "Elevation (m)") +
  ggtitle("Highest Elevation Points by County in New York State (2023)") +
  theme_bw()

#Highest county high point in New York State
highest_hp <- highpoints_df %>%
  slice_max(Elevation_Meters, n = 1)

#Lowest county high point in New York State
lowest_hp <- highpoints_df %>%
  slice_min(Elevation_Meters, n = 1)

#Print both together as a summary table
bind_rows(highest_hp, lowest_hp) %>%
  knitr::kable()

```


```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)

# Force the active R session to use your API key immediately
Sys.setenv(CENSUS_API_KEY = "9c9c7d071c8c8424a701ad68cc0b7fc6aa835ce2")

# 1. Load New York county populations from the US Census (ACS 5-Year Estimates)
ny_pop <- get_acs(
  geography = "county",
  variables = "B01003_001",
  state = "NY",
  year = 2023,
  geometry = TRUE
)

# 2. Shade each county by population using a light yellow to dark orange scale
ggplot(data = ny_pop) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = estimate), color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#ffffcc",
    high = "#d94701",
    labels = comma,
    name = "Population"
  ) +
  ggtitle("County Population in New York State (2023)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
# 1. Join population estimates to ny_gpkg (which already has ALAND) and calculate density

ny_density <- ny_gpkg %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(ny_pop), by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    area_sq_miles = set_units(ALAND, "m^2") %>% set_units("mi^2") %>% as.numeric(),
    pop_density = estimate / area_sq_miles)

# 2. Shade each county by population density (Light Lavender to Dark Purple)

ggplot(data = ny_density) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pop_density), color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#f2f0f7",
    high = "#54278f",
    labels = comma,
    name = "People / Sq Mi") +
  ggtitle("County Population Density in New York State") +
  theme_bw()

# 3. Summary table for largest/smallest population and most/least dense counties
summary_stats <- ny_density %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(
    `Largest Population` = NAME.x[which.max(estimate)],
    `Smallest Population` = NAME.x[which.min(estimate)],
    `Most Dense` = NAME.x[which.max(pop_density)],
    `Least Dense` = NAME.x[which.min(pop_density)])

knitr::kable(summary_stats)

#The largest county by population density is Kings County, which contains a population of 2.68 million residents. The smallest is
```
